stateError: The state file .docflow/state.json cannot be used ({detail}). Fix or delete it: it holds the approvals and the lock, not the documents.
stateBusy: Another docflow script is updating .docflow/state.json; try again in a moment.
configProblem: Option {key}: the value "{value}" ({source}) is not valid and was ignored.
invalidOption: The value "{value}" is not valid for {key}.
languageUnset: Per-project language removed from {file}: CLAUDE_PLUGINS_LANGUAGE, then /config, then English apply.
nextMissing: {doc} does not exist yet: {command} writes it.
nextDraft: {doc} is a draft: {command} completes it, then asks for its approval.
nextStale: {doc} is stale — a preceding document changed since its approval: {command} refreshes it.
nextClaudeMd: Every document is approved: {command} writes the docflow block of CLAUDE.md.
nextNone: Every document is approved and every task is ticked.
nextApprove: {doc} is complete: {command} checks it and records its approval.
gate: {doc} cannot start: {prev} is {status}, and it must be approved first. {command} completes it.
stageTwinsAdopted: {list}: written before docflow, taken as translated from the current English text; /docflow:translate sends only the sections changed from now on.
stageStale: {doc} is stale: revise it against the changed sections (CHANGED), then approve it again.
check_noTitle: the first line must be the title (# <Project> — <Title>).
check_noLimits: the last section, "{title}", should list the budgets or limits.
check_taskGrammar: not a task line docflow can read: "{line}".
check_badRef: {id} refers to {ref}, which does not exist.
approveRefused: {doc} is not approved: fix the problems above, then approve it again.
approvedStale: Now stale, to refresh in order: {list}.
claudeMd_created: The docflow block was added to CLAUDE.md.
claudeMd_updated: The docflow block of CLAUDE.md was refreshed.
claudeMd_unchanged: The docflow block of CLAUDE.md is already up to date.
claudeMd_absent: CLAUDE.md has no docflow block: /docflow:claude-md writes it.
unsupportedDocLanguage: Translations exist in fr, es and de, not "{value}".
translateNoLanguage: No translation is configured: set doc_languages (/config, or .docflow/config.json), or pass --lang.
translatePlan: {n} section(s) to translate: hand each SOURCE file to the translator, then apply its TARGET.
translateNothing: Every translation is up to date.
translateMissing: Sections missing from the translated file (they changed, or the twin lacks them): {list}. Nothing was written.
translateInvalid: These sections do not start with the heading level and number of the English ones: {list}. Nothing was written.
check_twinSectionMissing: section {section} is missing from the translation.
check_twinSectionExtra: section {section} no longer exists in English.
check_twinOutdated: section {section} was translated from an older English text.
nextPending: Nothing left to start: waiting for the draft pull request(s) {list} to be reviewed and merged.
noRun: No run in progress: /docflow:do next starts one.
runActive: Run {unit} is in progress ({status}): finish it first, or /docflow:do --resume.
doGate: TASKS.md is {status}: it must be approved before any implementation (/docflow:tasks, then /docflow:approve tasks).
docsUncommitted: The documents are not committed ({list}): the run's branch would not hold them. Commit them, or pass --commit-docs.
nothingNext: Nothing to implement: every task is ticked, or waits in a draft pull request.
unknownUnit: No sprint or task "{unit}" in TASKS.md.
dirtyTree: Tracked files have uncommitted changes: commit or stash them, or use --worktree.
lockBusy: Another session holds the docflow lock of this repository (since {since}, until {expires}): one run at a time.
lockExpired: The lock of another session expired at {expires}: ask the user, then pass --takeover to take it.
runStacked: Stacked on {unit} ({pr}), not merged yet: the branch starts from it.
runWorktreeMissing: The run's worktree {dir} no longer exists: /docflow:do abort, then start again.
checksUnset: No checks command: ask the user for the command that tests the project, then run config checks "<command>".
checksFailed: {command} failed for {id}; the run is stopped, its branch kept. Last {n} lines of the log:
notChecked: The checks have not passed for {id}: run do check {id} first.
changedSinceCheck: Files changed since the checks passed for {id}: run do check {id} again.
acceptanceNone: {sprint} has no acceptance test in TASKS.md.
noAcceptanceResult: The acceptance test of {sprint} has no recorded result: do acceptance {sprint}, then do result.
finished: Run {unit} finished: draft pull request {url}. Review it, then merge it yourself.
failedRecorded: {id} is recorded as failed; the branch is kept. {command} continues from there.
aborted: Run {unit} abandoned; the branch {branch} is kept.
issuesOff: The issues mirror is off. `config issues mirror` turns it on for this project (or the issues option in /config).
issuesRunActive: Run {unit} is in progress ({status}): the mirror writes TASKS.md, so finish the run first.
issuesNumbered: {n} issue number(s) written in {file} and its twins; the next run commits them.
issuesClosedOutside: {id}: issue #{number} is closed, the entry is not ticked.
issuesReopenedOutside: {id}: issue #{number} is open again, the entry is ticked.
issuesApplyHint: issues pull --apply ticks the closed ones and unticks the reopened ones, in TASKS.md and its twins.
issuesApplied: {file} and its twins now follow the issues.
guardMerge: gh pr merge is refused during a run: docflow opens draft pull requests and never merges; the user merges after review.
guardForce: A forced push (or a deletion) is refused during a run.
guardPushBase: Pushing to {base}, the default branch, is refused during a run: docflow pushes the run's branch itself (do finish).
guardCommitBase: Committing on {base}, the default branch, is refused during a run: work on the run's branch.
guardDoc: {file} is approved: it is changed only through its command (/docflow:{doc}), not during a run.
guardTasks: {file} is edited by docflow only (do commit, do result): never tick or edit it by hand.
guardStop: {id} is neither ticked nor reported as failed. Run do check {id} then do commit {id}; or, if it cannot be done, do fail {id} "<reason>".
guardSubagent: Nothing changed in the run's checkout for {id}: implement it, or say why no change is needed.
repoAlready: {dir} is already a git repository with commits.
repoEmpty: {dir} is a git repository without any commit, and this command needs one. `repo init --commit` commits the current files.
repoNoGit: git is not installed, or not on the PATH: this command needs it.
repoNoRemote: {dir} has no remote, and this command pushes a branch and opens a pull request through the GitHub CLI. `repo github` creates a private GitHub repository and pushes the code to it.
repoNone: {dir} is not a git repository, and this command needs one. `repo plan` shows what a first commit would hold; `repo init --commit` creates the repository.
repoNothingToCommit: Nothing to commit: the folder is empty, or everything is ignored.
repoPlanClean: Nothing looks like a secret, a key, a dependency or a build output.
repoPlanFiles: A first commit would hold {n} file(s) — the .gitignore applies.
repoPlanFlagged: Worth a look before committing (secrets, keys, dependencies, build output, large files):
